groups.distinction: Tras is a preposition with a direct complement; después can stand alone or take de + noun/infinitive. Luego overlaps with después as afterward and also has luego de / luego (de) que constructions. Entonces can locate an event at that time or introduce a consequence. These are not four mutually exclusive temporal meanings. DLE does not label the ordinary temporal tras sense formal.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use a short construction or a stated sense. A bare “afterward” still admits después/luego. A direct-complement frame distinguishes tras from bare después/luego, but not from the multiword alternatives después de/luego de. Do not label luego “sequence only”.

groups.distinction: Both mean begin and take a + infinitive. Krohn (2025) reports comenzar associated more with formal/written registers and empezar with informal/spoken registers, with country-level variation. These are useful teaching tendencies, not exclusive register meanings or grounds for rejecting either in an unrestricted beginning prompt.
groups.proposedTestApproach: A generic “to begin” or ordinary beginning example cannot fairly force one headword. Teach the pair together and explicitly acknowledge overlap.

groups.distinction: Saber includes factual knowledge and knowing how; conocer includes acquaintance/familiarity; entender includes comprehension. Their broader senses overlap. Comprender also means understand and can additionally mean include/comprise. A mandatory shallow/deep split between entender and comprender is unsupported.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use know how to swim / be acquainted with a person / understand an explanation as sense illustrations; validate exact sentence answers separately. The last still permits comprender.

groups.distinction: Pensar includes thinking through ideas; creer includes taking something as true; sentir includes sensations, emotions and regret. Importantly, sentir also has an opinion sense: it is not categorically excluded from “I feel/think that”. Considerar can mean deem/judge; parecer can express an impression.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Choose specific senses such as reflect on a problem, believe a claim, feel cold, or seem. Avoid claiming one exclusive translation for “think that”.

groups.distinction: Ser can identify/classify or attribute a property; estar presents a state or situation. Permanent versus temporary is not a reliable general rule.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use an identity/profession context versus a location/state context. Check adjective-dependent meaning changes; do not reduce the entire contrast to duration.

groups.distinction: The basic spatial contrast is near the speaker, near the addressee, and distant from both. Discourse reference and temporal uses extend beyond physical distance.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Give a speaker/listener reference, not just “that”. A compact “that, over there—far from both of us” cue can identify aquel.

groups.distinction: Por includes cause, route, means and exchange. Para includes intended purpose, destination, recipient and deadline. The dictionaries also record overlapping purpose uses; cause/purpose is a teaching entry point, not a complete partition.
groups.proposedTestApproach: State the particular relation: in exchange for, because of, intended for, or by a deadline. Check each sentence instead of sharing all answers to “for”.

groups.distinction: Dejar can leave something behind, abandon, permit or stop doing something; salir can exit/go out; irse can depart. Some departure senses overlap, but their constructions differ. Irse is a pronominal use of ir, not a separate Day 1 card.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Prefer leave an object behind / exit a room / go away, with the necessary object or construction visible. Do not pool all translations of “leave”.

groups.distinction: Lograr concerns achieving what one seeks; recibir concerns receiving; tener concerns possession/state. Conseguir overlaps strongly with lograr and obtaining; obtener also covers obtaining and extraction/production. These are not a clean effort/no-effort scale.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use achieve a desired result versus receive a delivery or possess something. Lograr/conseguir may remain valid together in an exact frame.

groups.distinction: Aún in the continuing-time sense corresponds to todavía; ya can mark already/now or, with negation, no longer; ahora anchors the present. Aun without the accent has other uses.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use “still, continuing up to now” rather than “now”; retain the accent. Do not invent a distinction from todavía for that sense.

groups.distinction: Tener expresses possession among other senses; haber forms compound tenses and existential expressions; existir expresses existence. English “have” or “be” alone hides these functions.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Separate “have as an auxiliary”, “have/possess”, and “exist”. A generic existential paraphrase may admit more than one construction.

groups.distinction: Basic motion senses confirmed: ir moves toward somewhere away from the speaker; venir toward the speaker’s location; llegar reaches an endpoint; entrar/salir cross inward/outward; volver returns and volver a repeats; pasar can cross, pass or happen. groups.distinction: Muy normally precedes noncomparative adjectives/adverbs; mucho modifies verbs and comparatives, and agrees when used as a determiner. groups.distinction: Siempre denotes all times; nunca no time/no occasion; cada distributes over members and can specify recurrence with a number and unit.
groups.proposedTestApproach: These are contrast/paraphrase candidates, not interchangeable one-word answers. Always and every time require different constructions; neither licenses changing negation. Proposed only; no new prompt or answer-list implementation.

groups.distinction: No negates; ni joins negative elements and also means not even in selected uses; sin marks absence and introduces negative infinitive expressions. Y adds/co-ordinates; o expresses alternatives or reformulation/equivalence.
groups.proposedTestApproach: “And/or” explanations describe selected functions; o need not be an exclusive choice. Negative concord is grammatical: adding no before a later negative item need not reverse meaning. Proposed only; no new prompt or answer-list implementation.

groups.distinction: Hasta marks an endpoint in time/space/quantity; desde a starting point; entre between/among or within; durante simultaneity over a period. Hasta also means even as an adverb.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Corrected: temporal hasta can mean not before in parts of the Americas. Do not turn an isolated deadline example into a universal polarity rule. Proposed only; no new prompt or answer-list implementation.

groups.distinction: Medio can be a means; sistema a system/method; manera and forma ways of doing something; así means in this way and como can introduce manner/comparison. These are different grammatical forms with overlapping descriptions.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Specify means/tool, organized method, manner noun or manner adverb. Do not use bare “way” for all of them.

groups.distinction: Primero/segundo are ordinals in the target cards; último is last; antes/después express relative order or time. Related ordering concepts are not interchangeable parts of speech.
groups.proposedTestApproach: State ordinal position versus before/after, and retain the requested headword form.

groups.distinction: Con can express accompaniment or an instrument; por can express means/channel. English “with/by” requires a particular relation.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Give the instrument or communication channel; do not map every use of “by” to por.

groups.distinction: Hoy refers to this day and also the present era. Ahora refers to this moment/current time and can extend to the recent past or near future.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Corrected: neither word has only its narrow calendar/moment sense. A clearly anchored this-day versus this-moment prompt can select the intended reading. Proposed only; no new prompt or answer-list implementation.

groups.distinction: Recordar retrieves or retains something in memory and can remind someone; saber is knowing. A remembered fact is also known, but “remember” and “know” do not test the same action.
groups.proposedTestApproach: Use recall a past event rather than know a fact; check the object and whether the intended meaning is remind.
